discovery: Prediction and experimental discovery of the spin Hall effect

nominees.name: Tomas Jungwirth
nominees.affiliation: Institute of Physics, Czech Academy of Sciences, Prague, Czech Republic

subfield: Condensed matter physics: spintronics and magnetism
motivation: Dyakonov (with the late V. I. Perel) predicted in 1971 that spin-orbit coupling deflects electrons of opposite spin to opposite sides of a conductor, producing a pure transverse spin current. In 2004-2005, Awschalom's group observed the resulting spin accumulation optically in semiconductors, and Jungwirth with Wunderlich and Sinova detected it with spin-LEDs in a two-dimensional hole gas. They also established the intrinsic mechanism that explains it. These results opened a new way to generate and detect spin currents without ferromagnets. The spin Hall effect and its inverse are now standard tools across condensed matter physics. They underlie spin-orbit torque switching, spin Hall nano-oscillators, spin pumping detection and spin caloritronics, and they are central to emerging SOT-MRAM technology. This is a basic relativistic effect in solids that has become an industrial technology, and its originators deserve recognition.
